correctness.rationale: All Omega=3 shapes are exhausted. Prime cubes fail by Fermat. Parity eliminates odd p^2q and even squarefree 2qr. For 4q, order constraints force every prime factor of q+2 into {3,5}; elementary valuations force both exponents at most one, giving q=3 or 13. For 2q^2, order constraints force q+2 to be a power of 3, but the 3-adic valuation of 2^(2q^2)-1 is exactly one. The witnesses 12 and 52 are checked directly.

value.rationale: The exact database already establishes that semiprimes are absent, so Omega=3 is the first possible multiplicity layer. Classifying its repeated-factor and parity branch is a natural structural refinement: only 12 and 52 occur, and all remaining first-layer solutions are forced to be odd squarefree triples. This is an unbounded exact classification rather than a finite table extension.
